articles.title: A slow day on Vaikom’s village waterways
articles.alt: Covered village boat on a green Vaikom canal
articles.intro: A boat moves under a canopy of green. On the bank, a village craft demonstration brings the morning ashore. This is the rhythm of Arafath’s full-day Vaikom experience.
sections: Begin on the water
Hotel pickup is between 8:30 and 8:45 AM. The tour includes a three-hour bamboo boat ride through Vaikom’s village backwaters, with time to notice the quieter scenes along the banks.
A village day, by hand

The programme includes coir rope making, mat weaving, coconut leaf weaving for thatched roofing and a handmade cloth weaving centre visit. These activities form part of the day rather than separate tours.
Lunch, then the smaller canals
A traditional Kerala lunch is included. Afterwards, a 45-minute small canal ride continues the backwater experience. Hotel drop-off is between 4:00 and 4:30 PM.
Arrange your visit
The tour operates daily at ₹1,900 per person. Send the team your preferred date, guest count and hotel name to confirm availability and pickup.

articles.title: Fort Kochi: fishing nets, heritage and the waterfront
articles.alt: Chinese fishing nets silhouetted at sunset in Fort Kochi, Kerala
articles.intro: Fort Kochi brings Kerala’s coastal heritage into a walkable waterfront setting. Traditional fishing nets and old streets make it a natural place to pause before a backwater trip.
sections: Start by the waterfront
The fishing nets are among Fort Kochi’s best-known sights. Give yourself time to watch the changing light and harbour activity rather than treating the waterfront as a quick photo stop.
Explore the heritage streets

Kerala Tourism highlights the area’s heritage monuments and the colonial history of Fort Kochi and Mattancherry. Combine the waterfront with a relaxed walk through the surrounding cultural neighbourhoods.
Make room in your itinerary

A separate Fort Kochi sightseeing outing can sit alongside your Vaikom day. Ask the team about a local cab route and the stops you would like to include; the village tour and sightseeing arrangements should be confirmed separately.

articles.title: Munnar: a quieter escape into Kerala’s hills
articles.alt: Green hills and a reservoir in the Munnar landscape, Kerala
articles.intro: Move inland and Kerala opens into a different landscape. Munnar’s valleys and hills offer a change of pace from the coast and backwaters.
sections: Let the landscape lead
Munnar is a hill retreat known for its scenery and biodiversity. Plan time for the landscape itself: hill views, quieter pauses and the journey between stops.
Give the hills their own day
Treat Munnar as a separate part of your Kerala itinerary rather than adding it to a full-day Vaikom tour. A relaxed plan leaves room for the road journey and the places you most want to see.
Arrange an outstation cab

Arafath’s cab service lists Munnar among its outstation destinations. Share your pickup location, dates, passenger count and desired stops with the team, then confirm the route and vehicle before travelling.

articles.title: Alappuzha: life along Kerala’s backwaters
articles.alt: Palm-lined Alappuzha backwaters reflected in still water, Kerala
articles.intro: Alappuzha, also known as Alleppey, is closely associated with Kerala’s network of waterways. Palms, villages and boats shape the landscape.
sections: Watch the banks as well as the water
Kerala Tourism’s backwater film highlights the villages and everyday life beside the canals. The attraction is not only the boat journey, but also the small scenes unfolding along it.
Choose the experience you want

An Alappuzha outing and Arafath’s Vaikom village tour are separate experiences. Vaikom’s published programme includes village crafts, lunch and two boat rides; confirm any Alappuzha boating arrangements independently.
Connect your Kerala stops
Alleppey is listed among Arafath’s outstation cab routes. Discuss your hotel, preferred departure and onward plans with the team, and confirm any separate boating arrangements before travelling.

articles.title: Athirappilly: Kerala’s waterfall country
articles.alt: Athirappilly waterfall flowing below forested hills in Kerala
articles.intro: At the entrance to the Sholayar forest ranges, Athirappilly presents another side of Kerala: a broad waterfall surrounded by a lush landscape.
sections: A landscape worth slowing down for
Kerala Tourism describes Athirappilly as Kerala’s largest waterfall of its kind, dropping roughly 80 feet. The surrounding greenery is part of the experience, not simply a backdrop.
Plan a separate nature outing
Keep a waterfall visit separate from the Vaikom full-day programme. Confirm current access and local conditions before setting out, and allow time to enjoy the designated viewing areas.
Ask about a custom journey
If Athirappilly is on your list, ask the team whether a custom cab itinerary can be arranged for your travel date. Availability and the final route are confirmed directly with Arafath Tours.

articles.title: Kerala lunch and the craft of village life
articles.alt: Kerala sadya dishes served on a banana leaf
articles.intro: Food and handmade traditions give a backwater day its local character. In the Vaikom tour, a Kerala lunch sits between village craft visits and the smaller canal ride.
sections: Craft traditions along the way
See coir rope making, mat weaving, coconut leaf weaving and a handmade cloth weaving centre. The client’s gallery shows guests observing and taking part in village demonstrations.
Pause for Kerala lunch

Traditional Kerala lunch is included in the published tour. The photograph shows a Kerala sadya, the banana-leaf feast associated with the region; the exact tour menu should be confirmed with the team.
Tell us what you need
Mention dietary requirements when making your enquiry. After lunch, the programme continues with a 45-minute small canal ride before the hotel return.
